penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: Hybrid Exchange migration remediation requires reading environment-specific PowerShell outputs, AAD states, and EWS error logs that vary per tenant — each case needs a human (or at minimum a deeply interactive Claude session) to diagnose and advise. Pure automation is not feasible without direct environment access.

penalties_applied.name: requires_synchronous_human
penalties_applied.reason: Sysadmins hitting live migration errors need real-time back-and-forth diagnosis, not an async document delivery — this naturally pulls toward live support or synchronous consulting.

rationale: IT admins in mid-migration crises are a named, funded buyer (companies already paying Microsoft E3/E5 licensing) and the pain is genuine and expensive — consultants charge $150-300/hr for this exact work. However, the service cannot run autonomously: each hybrid Exchange failure is tenant-specific, requires live diagnostic access or at minimum a detailed interactive session, and demands real-time remediation guidance. The two penalties for human fulfillment and synchronous interaction correctly disqualify this for a hands-off Claude factory; it is a consulting engagement, not a scalable product.
solution_plan: Not recommended to pursue as an automated micro-service. A solo non-technical operator cannot build tooling that connects to customer Azure/Exchange tenants, runs PowerShell diagnostics, and delivers safe remediation steps without deep IT infrastructure access and real-time loops. The factory could produce a Claude-powered diagnostic runbook document sold one-time, but that underserves the pain (sysadmins need interactive diagnosis, not a static guide) and would generate low recurring revenue. Better left to specialist IT MSPs.
notes: Fails operational_autonomy_min (4 < 7) and buildability_with_ai_min (5 < 6) build gates. Total after penalties also well below validate threshold.
